restrictions: Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes each; complete SHA-256 with the standard IV, steps 0..30 on all three padded blocks, full feed-forward and all 256 digest bits. M1 and M1' differ in words 5..9.

Published attack structure (Mendel-Nad-Schlaeffer 2013; Li-Liu-Wang 2024; Li-Liu-Wang-Dong-Sun 2024), but no published characteristic, starting point or colliding pair is used: the characteristic is produced by the authors' public correct_dc_model_31_256 model solved with STP, selected among 9 measured outputs, and all of that solver work is charged.

All solver work (6829.6 CPU-seconds) is charged under H-CONV at 2^26 units per CPU-second; all other preprocessing (160,000 starting points, 1,161,880 tuples, completions, word sets, tables) is charged by instrumented operation counts.

Each of exactly N = 96*2^30 trials draws its first block from two fresh independent uniform 256-bit RAM words; hard caps on key hits (2^25), prefix-valid trials (2^19) and completion calls (2^15, each with at most 2^18 x and 2^14 z candidates) make the time bound hold for every run.

The per-trial success probability under a uniform chaining value is a fixed-table quantity bounded with an exact overlap-correct Karp-Luby estimator and a Clopper-Pearson bound (H-SAMPLING); H1 relates the real chaining-value distribution to the uniform one with a factor-2 slack.

Unused or aborted computations (an earlier find_dc_model run whose outputs admitted no starting point, earlier solver formulations, duplicate deterministic search runs aborted by implementation bugs) produced no input to the algorithm; they are disclosed in proof Section 13 and not charged.
The baseline_improved identifier is required metadata naming the organizer's nominal reference; comparison with the Yukon incumbent is left to Yukon.

heuristics.statement: One CPU-second of the STP/CryptoMiniSat runs charged in proof Section 3 costs at most 2^26 collision-frontier-v5 units, i.e. at most 2^37.06 primitive 256-bit word operations.
heuristics.scope: Only the measured solver CPU time (6829.6 CPU-seconds) that produced and selected the characteristic and the base starting point. All other preprocessing and online work is charged by counted operations.
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware basis: Intel Core i5-12450H, maximum clock 4.4 GHz, at most 8 instructions retired per cycle, so at most 3.52e10 instructions per CPU-second; premise that a 256-bit word RAM simulates the average executed x86-64 instruction of these solvers in at most 4 word operations. Our dense scalar 31-step compression runs at about 2^33.5 word operations per CPU-second, 12 times below the bound.
heuristics.limitations: No hardware instruction counters were available (perf disabled), so the instruction rate is bounded, not measured, and the ops-per-instruction factor is a modeling premise. Sensitivity: at 2^27 units per CPU-second the total would be 2^40.07.

heuristics.statement: For CV = C(IV, M0) with a uniform 512-bit block M0 and the fixed tables of proof Section 6: (a) the per-trial success probability is at least half of its value under a uniform 256-bit CV; (b) the prefix-valid probability is at most 2^4 times its uniform value.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target and the fixed table of 1,161,880 tuples from 160,000 starting points with their completions. Trial independence holds because first blocks are fresh coins.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured in a full run of this algorithm (2^37.56 trials): 32-bit key hits 45,267,325 vs 45,262,421 expected; 41-bit key+W6 events 107,435 vs 106,986; prefix-valid trials (per-tuple measure 2^-49.86) 228 vs 227.1; collisions 3 vs 2.2. Extrapolated to the success event at the claimed trial count.
heuristics.limitations: Our run, not organizer-executed. Prefix-valid counts are well matched, but only 3 successes were observed, so a small-factor deviation at the full success event is not excluded; the factor-2 slack covers this. Sensitivity: rho = 0.45 instead of 1/2 gives success 0.382.

heuristics.statement: The probability that A_-1 of the real chaining value is one of the 960,237 table keys is at most 1.2 times its uniform value.
heuristics.scope: Only the key-hit cap failure term (below 1e-6 under this premise).
heuristics.extrapolation: Directly sampled at high count: 45,267,325 key hits vs 45,262,421 expected (ratio 1.0001) over 2^37.56 real trials.

heuristics.statement: The ChaCha20 keystream words used by our estimator of E[I] behave as independent uniform samples, so the exact Clopper-Pearson bound E[I] >= 0.009458 at alpha = 1e-9 applies (48,593 successes in 5,000,000 samples).
heuristics.scope: Only the sampling program estimating the fixed-table quantity E[I]; the attack's own coins are fresh uniform RAM words by definition.
heuristics.extrapolation: ChaCha20 is a standard stream cipher with no known distinguisher; the implementation matches the RFC 8439 test vector; two independent seeds gave consistent rates (0.009741 and 0.009713).
heuristics.limitations: The estimator is our own program and not organizer-executed. The success bound falls below 0.39 only if E[I] < 0.00874, about 10% below the estimate 0.009719 and about 22 standard errors away.
